# Importing and Merging Data

```{r import}

#In this chunk we are importing data 

#set working directory
setwd("C:/Users/igrossma/Dropbox/Community 1.0 Raw Files/")

#setwd("C:/Users/mypc/Dropbox/Community 1.0 Raw Files/Clean Code for OSF")

#import main dataset
TEST <- read.csv('Clean Code for OSF/Study1.anonymizeddata.csv') 

#import attrition data
attrition <- read.csv('CSV/attrition.csv')

type<-read.csv('CSV/PrelabIGI.csv')

Output.combined <- read.csv("CSV/Condition.manip.check_May7_2019.csv")
#import coded responses to check manipulation for distancing

event.codes<-read.csv("CSV/eventcodes.csv")
```


```{r merge.data}

#Here we join TEST dataframe with attrition dataframe using subjectNumber variable
TEST <- TEST %>% left_join(attrition, by = c("subjectNumber"))
TEST <- TEST %>% left_join(type, by = c("subjectNumber"))

#Here we join TEST dataframe with the codes of the event types between Intake and Outtake lab session
#included are: repeated person, place type and conflict type
TEST <- TEST %>% left_join(event.codes, by = c("subjectNumber","SurveyType"))


```




## Data Cleaning

```{r delete.repeats}

#In this chunk we are correcting repeated events flag variable

#Get the index of missing values in the Repeat.event variable  
repeat.na <- which(is.na(TEST$Repeat.event))

#Replace missing values with 0
TEST$Repeat.event[repeat.na] <- 0


```


```{r recode.vars}

#In this chunk we are creating new recoded condition and demographics variables

#Create Time.D varible such that "Intake" rows are coded as 0 - all the remaining rows are automatically set as NA by R.
TEST$Time.D[TEST$SurveyType=="Intake"] <- 0

#Populate Time.D rows with 1s where SurveyType is "Outtake" - basically recode all Outtake rows into 1 
TEST$Time.D[TEST$SurveyType=="Outtake"] <- 1

#Recode Condition.D variable valus from 1 to 0 and from 3 to 1.  
TEST$Condition.D[TEST$Condition.D==1] <- 0
TEST$Condition.D[TEST$Condition.D==3] <- 1

#Recode gender into a categorical character vector 
TEST$gender[TEST$sex==1]<-"male"
TEST$gender[TEST$sex==2]<-"female"
TEST$gender[TEST$sex==3]<-"other"

#Create a dichotomous adversity score variable where 0 adversity events is coded as 0 and more than 0 is coded as 1. 
TEST$adversity[TEST$adverse.events == "0"] <- 0 
TEST$adversity[TEST$adverse.events > 0] <- 1 


#Recode time of the day variable, such that "don't remember" is omitted
TEST$time[TEST$time==0] <- NA


```



```{r Create factor-level predictors}

#In this chunk we mean center predictors and declare the main ones as factors

#NOTE: adding as.numeric() for 2 reasons: 1). to drop attributes that the scale function creates and 2). to force the newly created variable to be a vector and not a matrix

#DECLARE FACTORS

#Make Time into a factor and save it into a new variable: Time.F
TEST$Time.F <- factor(TEST$Time.D)

#Make a new Condition.F factor variable from Condition.D one
TEST$Condition.F <- factor(TEST$Condition.D)

```



```{r exclude.no.events}

#In this chunk we create a smaller dataset for analyses that only contains participants who reflected on at least two events, per pre-registration.

TEST <- subset(TEST, refl.event > 1)

```



```{r convert.to.long}

#In this chunk we convert our existing dataset to long format with the coded wisdom scores for each dimension and coder converted from columns to rows

#Create a character vector of all wisdom dimension variable names by coder
wr.all <- c("Limits_NJ", "Limits_OT", "Change_NJ", "Change_OT", "Perspective_Taking_NJ", "Perspective_Taking_OT", "Compromise_NJ", "Compromise_OT", "Search_for_Resolution_NJ", "Search_for_Resolution_OT")

#Convert to long
TEST_lg <- gather(TEST, key = "dimension", value = "score", wr.all, na.rm = TRUE)


```



```{r recode.dimension}

#In this chunk we created new recoded variables for coders and wisdom dimensions

##Create a new variable "coder" which will contain 1s and 0s for the two coders
TEST_lg$coder[TEST_lg$dimension == "Limits_NJ"] <- 1
TEST_lg$coder[TEST_lg$dimension == "Limits_OT"] <- 0
TEST_lg$coder[TEST_lg$dimension == "Change_NJ"] <- 1
TEST_lg$coder[TEST_lg$dimension == "Change_OT"] <- 0
TEST_lg$coder[TEST_lg$dimension == "Perspective_Taking_NJ"] <- 1
TEST_lg$coder[TEST_lg$dimension == "Perspective_Taking_OT"] <- 0
TEST_lg$coder[TEST_lg$dimension == "Compromise_NJ"] <- 1
TEST_lg$coder[TEST_lg$dimension == "Compromise_OT"] <- 0
TEST_lg$coder[TEST_lg$dimension == "Search_for_Resolution_NJ"] <- 1
TEST_lg$coder[TEST_lg$dimension == "Search_for_Resolution_OT"] <- 0

##Create a new variable "aspect" which will contain a character vector for each wisdom dimension
TEST_lg$aspect[TEST_lg$dimension=="Limits_NJ"] <- "IH"
TEST_lg$aspect[TEST_lg$dimension=="Limits_OT"] <- "IH"
TEST_lg$aspect[TEST_lg$dimension=="Change_NJ"] <- "Chg"
TEST_lg$aspect[TEST_lg$dimension=="Change_OT"] <- "Chg"
TEST_lg$aspect[TEST_lg$dimension=="Perspective_Taking_NJ"] <- "Prsp"
TEST_lg$aspect[TEST_lg$dimension=="Perspective_Taking_OT"] <- "Prsp"
TEST_lg$aspect[TEST_lg$dimension=="Compromise_NJ"] <- "Comp"
TEST_lg$aspect[TEST_lg$dimension=="Compromise_OT"] <- "Comp"
TEST_lg$aspect[TEST_lg$dimension=="Search_for_Resolution_NJ"] <- "Reso"
TEST_lg$aspect[TEST_lg$dimension=="Search_for_Resolution_OT"] <- "Reso"


```


```{r check.score}

#Here check the skew of coded wisdom scores and use the Normalize function to create a new less skewed variable  

#histogram of score
hist(TEST_lg$score) #variable skewed 

skewness(TEST_lg$score)

#Normalized histogram of score
hist(Normalize(TEST_lg$score)) # use normalize function below, though still skewed

#Create a new score.norm variable that contains the Normalized scores
TEST_lg$score.norm <- Normalize(TEST_lg$score)
skewness(TEST_lg$score.norm)

```


#test-retest reliability of wise reasoning
```{r icc}
#examine within-person reliability of wise reasoning (IRR is % of within-person variance)

model.WR.irr <- lmer(coded.wiz ~ (1|subjectNumber), data = TEST)
summ(model.WR.irr) #sqrt of icc showed correlation across timepoints 
```

# Main Analyses

##Disctiminant analyses of wise reasoning
```{r correlations with SWIS}
SWS<-c("SWSa_1" ,                   "SWSa_2"                    , "SWSa_3",                    "SWSa_4",                   "SWSa_5",                   "SWSa_6",                   "SWSa_7","SWSa_8",                   
 "SWSb_1"   ,                  "SWSb_2"       ,              "SWSb_3"   ,                  "SWSb_4",                    
 "SWSb_5"  ,                   "SWSb_6"      ,               "SWSc_1" ,               
 "SWSc_2" ,                    "SWSc_3" )
TEST$SWS<-rowMeans(TEST[SWS])
perspect <- c("SWSa_1", "SWSa_2", "SWSa_3", "SWSa_4")
change <- c("SWSa_5", "SWSa_6", "SWSa_7", "SWSa_8")
humility <- c("SWSb_1", "SWSb_2", "SWSb_3", "SWSb_4")
compr <- c("SWSb_5", "SWSb_6","SWSc_1")
resol<-c("SWSc_2", "SWSc_3")
TEST$SWS.perspect<-rowMeans(TEST[perspect])
TEST$SWS.change<-rowMeans(TEST[change])
TEST$SWS.humility<-rowMeans(TEST[humility])
TEST$SWS.compr<-rowMeans(TEST[compr])
TEST$SWS.resol<-rowMeans(TEST[resol])

#get complementary dichotomous (present vs. not present for each theme, as well as sum across)
TEST$Limits2[TEST$Limits==1]<-0 
TEST$Limits2[TEST$Limits>1]<-1

TEST$Change2[TEST$Change==1]<-0 
TEST$Change2[TEST$Change>1]<-1

TEST$Perspective_Taking2[TEST$Perspective_Taking==1]<-0 
TEST$Perspective_Taking2[TEST$Perspective_Taking>1]<-1

TEST$Compromise2[TEST$Compromise==1]<-0 
TEST$Compromise2[TEST$Compromise>1]<-1

TEST$Search_for_Resolution[TEST$Search_for_Resolution==1]<-0 
TEST$Search_for_Resolution2[TEST$Search_for_Resolution>1]<-1

score2<-c("Limits2","Change2","Perspective_Taking2","Compromise2","Compromise2")
TEST$dichotom.wisdom<-rowSums(TEST[score2])
TEST$wise.reasoning<-TEST$coded.wiz
TEST$Raven<-TEST$APM_corr
TEST$SWISS<-TEST$SWS
TEST$neg.emodiversity<-TEST$ED.neg.res.h
TEST$pos.emodiversity<-TEST$ED.pos.res.h


#results for total wise reasoning
corr.test(TEST[c("wise.reasoning","dichotom.wisdom","Raven","SWISS","neg.emodiversity","pos.emodiversity")], method="spearman",adjust="none")

corr.test(TEST[c("Limits","SWS.humility","Change","SWS.change","Perspective_Taking","SWS.perspect","Compromise","SWS.compr","Search_for_Resolution","SWS.resol")], method="spearman",adjust="none")

corr.test(TEST[c("Limits2","SWS.humility","Change2","SWS.change","Perspective_Taking2","SWS.perspect","Compromise2","SWS.compr","Search_for_Resolution2","SWS.resol")], method="spearman",adjust="none")


```

## Effect of Condition and Time on Wise Reasoning

```{r main.analyses}

#Test linear mixed effects with normalized scores (still skewed) - Effect of Time and Condition

#Model Fit
model.WR.codedX <- lmer(score.norm ~ Time.F * Condition.F + (1|subjectNumber)+(1|aspect)+(1|coder), data = TEST_lg)

model.WR.codedX.C <- lmer(score.norm ~ Time.D * Condition.D + (1|subjectNumber)+(1|aspect)+(1|coder), data = TEST_lg)
summary(model.WR.codedX.C)

#model summary
summ(model.WR.codedX.C, digits = 7, center = "all")

#get effect size for the interaction
t_to_eta2(2.7024849, df_error = 2638.0200046) #etasq = .00276



#test distribution of residuals
plot(model.WR.codedX, re.form = NULL) 

#Simple effects
test1<-(emmeans(model.WR.codedX, ~Time.F| Condition.F)) #sig effect
test2<-(emmeans(model.WR.codedX, ~ Condition.F|Time.F)) #sig effect

#contrast, adjusting for false discovery rate
contrast(test1,interaction=T,adjust="fdr") #growth by type
summ(lmer(Normalize(score) ~ Time.F + (1|subjectNumber)+(1|aspect)+(1|coder), data = subset(TEST_lg, Condition.F=="1")),digits=7) #Rsq - .014
summ(lmer(Normalize(score) ~ Time.F + (1|subjectNumber)+(1|aspect)+(1|coder), data = subset(TEST_lg, Condition.F=="0")),digits=7) #Rsq - .00004


contrast(test2,interaction=T,adjust="fdr") #effects of condition before and after - not significant
summ(lmer(Normalize(score) ~ Condition.F  + (1|subjectNumber)+(1|aspect)+(1|coder), data = subset(TEST_lg, Time.F=="0")),digits=7) #BEFORE Rsq - 002
summ(lmer(Normalize(score) ~ Condition.F  + (1|subjectNumber)+(1|aspect)+(1|coder), data = subset(TEST_lg, Time.F=="1")),digits=7) #BEFORE Rsq - 002

t_to_eta2(1.143, df_error = 197) # BEFORE.00659 => .01
t_to_eta2(1.173, df_error = 240) # AFTER.00570=> .01



```


```{r examine effects of condition and time on wise reasoning average - to compare effect size}

skewness(TEST$wise.reasoning)
hist(TEST$wise.reasoning) #variable highly skewed (apply inverse gamma model - to test simple effects, )

model.wise.reasoning <- lmer(1/wise.reasoning ~ Time.D * Condition.D + (1|subjectNumber), data = TEST)
summ(model.wise.reasoning, center="all", digits=4)

r2beta(model.wise.reasoning, method = 'sgv', partial = TRUE) #Rsq = .006

contrast(regrid(emmeans(model.wise.reasoning,  ~Time.D|Condition.D )),interaction=T, lmer.df="kenward-roger")
t_to_eta2(2.651, df_error = 247, digits=4) #etasq  = .03
summ(lmer(1/wise.reasoning ~ Time.F  + (1|subjectNumber), data = subset(TEST,Condition.F=="1")), digits=4) #distanced etasq = .04
summ(lmer(1/wise.reasoning ~ Time.F  + (1|subjectNumber), data = subset(TEST,Condition.F=="0")), digits=4) #control etasq = .0009


model.wise.reasoning <- lmer(Normalize(wise.reasoning) ~ Time.D * Condition.D + (1|subjectNumber), data = TEST)
summ(model.wise.reasoning, center="all", digits=4)
contrast(regrid(emmeans(model.wise.reasoning,  ~Time.D|Condition.D )),interaction=T, lmer.df="kenward-roger")
t_to_eta2(2.368, df_error = 248, digits=4) #etasq  = .02
summ(lmer(Normalize(wise.reasoning) ~ Time.F  + (1|subjectNumber), data = subset(TEST,Condition.F=="1")), digits=4) #distanced etasq = .03
summ(lmer(Normalize(wise.reasoning) ~ Time.F  + (1|subjectNumber), data = subset(TEST,Condition.F=="0")), digits=4) #control etasq = .002


```

##multiverse analyses involving different distributions (Gamma, Bayesian ordinal multilevel model) and different coding (presense vs. no presense of a wisdom theme)
```{r dichotomous codes}

#rerun with generalized estimator and gamma distribution (better correction for the skew)
model.WR.codedX.gamma <- glmer(score ~ Time.F * Condition.F + (1|coder) + (1|subjectNumber) , data = TEST_lg,  family = Gamma)
#model summary
summ(model.WR.codedX.gamma, exp  =  TRUE, digits = 4,  center  =  TRUE)

#test distribution of residuals - slighly better fit
plot(model.WR.codedX.gamma,  re.form  =  NULL) 
plot_model(model.WR.codedX.gamma, type="int")

#rerun with gamma distribution
emmeans(model.WR.codedX.gamma, pairwise~Time.F| Condition.F) #sig effect


#try the Bayesian model (version 3) with ordinal data
library("rstan")
library(brms)
library(tidybayes)
library(tidyverse)
model.WR.codedX.bayes <- brm(score ~ Time.F * Condition.F + (1|subjectNumber), data = TEST_lg,  family = cumulative(), iter=3000)
model.WR.codedX.bayes1 <- brm(score ~ Time.F * Condition.F + (1|subjectNumber), data = TEST_lg,  family = acat())

summary(model.WR.codedX.bayes)
summary(model.WR.codedX.bayes1)

conditions <- data.frame(make_conditions(model.WR.codedX.bayes1, "Condition.F"))
labels.cond<-c("Control","Training")

plot(conditional_effects(model.WR.codedX.bayes1, "Time.F",conditions=conditions,categorical=T),plot = FALSE)[[1]] + 
  theme_nice() + theme(legend.title = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom") + scale_x_discrete(labels = c("Before", "After")) +scale_color_colorblind() +
  scale_fill_colorblind()+labs(x="")+facet_grid(.~ Condition.F)

#rerun with 3-4 being one category
TEST_lg$score34[TEST_lg$score==1]<-1
TEST_lg$score34[TEST_lg$score==2]<-2
TEST_lg$score34[TEST_lg$score==3]<-3
TEST_lg$score34[TEST_lg$score==4]<-3
TEST_lg$score34[TEST_lg$score==5]<-4

model.WR.codedX.gamma34 <- glmer(score34 ~ Time.F * Condition.F + (1|subjectNumber) + (1|coder), data = TEST_lg,  family = Gamma)
#model summary
summ(model.WR.codedX.gamma34, exp  =  TRUE, digits = 4,  center  =  TRUE)
plot_model(model.WR.codedX.gamma34, type="int")

model.WR.codedX.bayes34 <- brm(score34 ~ Time.F * Condition.F + (1|subjectNumber), data = TEST_lg,  family = acat())

summary(model.WR.codedX.bayes34)
conditions <- make_conditions(model.WR.codedX.bayes34, "Condition.F")
plot(conditional_effects(model.WR.codedX.bayes34, "Time.F",conditions=conditions,categorical=T),plot = FALSE)[[1]] + 
  theme_nice() + theme(legend.title = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom") + scale_x_discrete(labels = c("Before", "After")) +scale_color_colorblind() +
  scale_fill_colorblind()+labs(x="")+facet_grid(.~ Condition.F)

#try with dichotomous (no mentioning of a theme vs. mentioning of a theme)

TEST_lg$score2[TEST_lg$score==1]<-0
TEST_lg$score2[TEST_lg$score>1]<-1

model.WR.codedX.binom <- glmer(score2 ~ Time.F * Condition.F + (1|subjectNumber) + (1|coder), data = TEST_lg,  family = binomial)
emmeans(model.WR.codedX.binom, pairwise~Time.F| Condition.F) #sig effect
  
  summ(model.WR.codedX.binom,digits=3) #significant effect, close to the effect of the gamma model
plot_model(model.WR.codedX.binom, type="int")

```


##Control for type of event - same person at time 1 and 2, location, and conflict type

```{r event controls}

#Model Fit
model.WR.codedX.event <- lmer(score.norm ~ Time.F * Condition.F+ same.person+where.code+event.code.final+(1|coder) + (1|subjectNumber)+(1|aspect), data = TEST_lg)

#model summary
summ(model.WR.codedX.event, digits = 4, center = "all")

t_to_eta2(2.8037    , df_error = 2652.9804) # with controls .00295

summ(lmer(Normalize(score) ~ Time.F + same.person+where.code+event.code.final+(1|coder) + (1|subjectNumber)+(1|aspect), data = subset(TEST_lg, Condition.F=="1")),digits=7) #distanced Rsq =  0.0363413
summ(lmer(Normalize(score) ~ same.person+where.code+event.code.final+(1|coder) + (1|subjectNumber)+(1|aspect), data = subset(TEST_lg, Condition.F=="1")),digits=7) #distanced Rsq =  0.0258121
#r of time: sqrt(0.0363413 -0.0258121) = 0.1026119

summ(lmer(Normalize(score) ~ Time.F + same.person+where.code+event.code.final+ (1|subjectNumber)+(1|aspect), data = subset(TEST_lg, Condition.F=="0")),digits=5) #control [get rid of random intercept for coder due to icc =0 and convergence issues] rsq = 0.07355
summ(lmer(Normalize(score) ~  same.person+where.code+event.code.final+ (1|subjectNumber)+(1|aspect), data = subset(TEST_lg, Condition.F=="0")),digits=5) #control [get rid of random intercept for coder due to icc =0 and convergence issues] rsq = 0.07246
#r = sqrt(0.07355 - 0.07246)  = 0.03301515

t_to_r(0.88683             , df_error = 1269.74725      ) # etasq control with controls .0006

plot_model(model.WR.codedX.event,type="int")
emmeans(model.WR.codedX.event,pairwise~where.code) #greater wisdom for conflicts that happened at Uni than at home
emmeans(model.WR.codedX.event,pairwise~event.code.final) #greater wisdom for close relationship vs. family conflicts/ friends vs. others / close relationships vs. others / close relationships vs. work colleagues

```


## Effect of Condition and Time on Wise Reasoning with further controls

```{r main.analyses.with.controls}

TEST_lg$age.c <- scale(TEST_lg$age, scale = F)

#In this chunk we check to see if the effect of condition and time holds when controlling for  event- and diary-specific contextual differences
model.WR.codedX.control <- lmer(score.norm ~ Time.D * Condition.D + weekday+time + length + streamwords + adverse.events + (1|subjectNumber)  + (1|aspect)+ (1|coder), data = TEST_lg, REML = T)

#summary of the model
summ(model.WR.codedX.control, digits = 4, center = "all")
t_to_eta2(3.1891                   , df_error = 2468.9929            ) # etasq control with controls .004

#control for demographics and individual differences in IQ
model.WR.codedX.control1 <- lmer(score.norm ~ Time.D * Condition.D + age.c + factor(gender) + factor(race) + APM_corr + (1|subjectNumber)  + (1|aspect)+ (1|coder), data = TEST_lg, REML = T)

#model summary
summ(model.WR.codedX.control1, digits = 8, center = "all") #Rsq 0.03706125
summ(lmer(score.norm ~ age.c + factor(gender) + factor(race) + APM_corr + (1|subjectNumber)  + (1|aspect)+ (1|coder), data = TEST_lg, REML = T), digits=7) # Rsq 0.0325975

t_to_r(3.50832707                         , df_error = 2356.62824221                  , digits=5) # etasq control with controls .005

```

## Main Graph PANEL A

```{r main.graph Panel A}

TEST_lg$Time.F <- factor(TEST_lg$Time.D, labels = c("Before", "After"))

##GRAPH for the MAIN PAPER
##first, rerun model with categorical predictors:
model.WR.coded_C <- lmer(score.norm ~ Time.F * Condition.F + (1|coder) + (1|subjectNumber), data = TEST_lg, REML = T)

plot1 <- interactions::cat_plot(model.WR.coded_C, Condition.F, Time.F, geom = "point", pred.point.size = 5.5, interval.geom = "errorbar", errorbar.width = 0, centered = "all", robust = T, x.label = "Condition", y.label = "Estimate +/- 95 CI", colors = "Set1", pred.labels = c("Control", "Training"))

plotX <- plot1 + theme_nice()+theme(legend.title = element_blank(), legend.justification = c(1, 0), legend.position = c(1, 0.01)) + ylim(1.1, 2) + guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size=4.5))) + scale_x_discrete(labels = c("Control", "Training")) +scale_colour_colorblind()


TEST_lg$Time.F <- factor(TEST_lg$Time.D, labels = c("Before", "After"))


#get scores for proportion of each level
TEST_lg$score.F <- factor(TEST_lg$score)
TEST_lg$Condition.X <- factor(TEST_lg$Condition.F, labels = c("Control", "Training"))

TEST_lg %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(aspect), group = score.F, fill = score.F)) + 
  geom_bar(position = "fill")+  facet_wrap(~Condition.X+Time.F, scales = "free")+ scale_fill_colorblind()+
theme_nice()+
  theme(legend.position="top")+labs(fill="Level of Wise Reasoning",x = "Level of Wise Reasoning", y = "Proportion")


# Main
data.means <- ggpredict(model.WR.coded_C, terms = c("Condition.F", "Time.F"))
data.means$Condition[data.means$x==0] <- "First Person Control"
data.means$Condition[data.means$x==1] <- "Third Person Training"
data.means <- as.data.frame(data.means)

plotMain <- ggplot(data.means, aes(group, predicted, colour=Condition))+labs(y="Mean +/- 95% CI")+
  geom_line(position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), aes(group = Condition), size = 0.7, alpha = 1, linetype = "dotted") +
  scale_color_manual(values =  c("#E69F00", "#440154FF")) +  jtools::theme_nice() + theme(legend.position = "none") + theme(axis.title.x = element_text(size = 14)) + 
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high), position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), size = 0.8) +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), size = 5.5) +  xlab("Wisdom") + scale_x_discrete(labels = c("Before", "After")) + 
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(1.1,2)) + 
  theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 12), axis.title.y = element_text(size = 14), legend.text = element_text(size = 10))
```

## MAIN GRAPH SUB_DIMENSION GRAPHS + supplementary analyses for each dimension
### Coded Wisdom Dimensions


```{r long.datasets.wisdom}

#In this chunk we create 5 separate datasets for each wisdom dimension with coder variables converted to rows.

#Create a vector for each wisdom dimension by coder 
limits.all <- c("Limits_NJ", "Limits_OT")
change.all <- c("Change_OT","Change_OT")
perspective.all <- c("Perspective_Taking_NJ", "Perspective_Taking_OT")
compromise.all <- c("Compromise_NJ", "Compromise_OT")
resolution.all <- c("Search_for_Resolution_NJ", "Search_for_Resolution_OT")

TEST$Time.F <- as.factor(TEST$Time.F)

TEST_limits_lg <- gather(TEST, key = "coder", value = "score", limits.all, na.rm = T)
TEST_change_lg <- gather(TEST, key = "coder", value = "score", change.all, na.rm = T)
TEST_perspective_lg <- gather(TEST, key = "coder", value = "score", perspective.all, na.rm = T)
TEST_compromise_lg <- gather(TEST, key = "coder", value = "score", compromise.all, na.rm = T)
TEST_resolution_lg <- gather(TEST, key = "coder", value = "score", resolution.all, na.rm = T)

```


```{r main.analyses.by.dimension}

#In this chunk we examine whether the interaction of Condition by Time stands for each individual dimension of wisdom.

#Normalize wisdom scores for each dimension 
TEST_limits_lg$score.norm <- Normalize(TEST_limits_lg$score)
TEST_change_lg$score.norm <- Normalize(TEST_change_lg$score)
TEST_perspective_lg$score.norm <- Normalize(TEST_perspective_lg$score)
TEST_compromise_lg$score.norm <- Normalize(TEST_compromise_lg$score)
TEST_resolution_lg$score.norm <- Normalize(TEST_resolution_lg$score)


#Test the main interaction finding for each dimension

###LIMITS
model.WR.coded.limits <- lmer(score.norm ~ Time.F * Condition.F + (1|subjectNumber),data = TEST_limits_lg, REML = T)

summ(lmer(Normalize(score) ~ Time.F  + (1|subjectNumber)  , data = subset(TEST_limits_lg, Condition.F=="1")), digits=4) #distanced condition
summ(lmer(Normalize(score) ~ Time.F  + (1|subjectNumber)  , data = subset(TEST_limits_lg, Condition.F=="0")), digits=4) #control condition

###CHANGE
model.WR.coded.change <- lmer(score.norm ~ Time.F * Condition.F + (1|subjectNumber),data = TEST_change_lg, REML = T)
summ(lmer(Normalize(score) ~ Time.F  + (1|subjectNumber)  , data = subset(TEST_change_lg, Condition.F=="1")), digits=4) #distanced condition
summ(lmer(Normalize(score) ~ Time.F  + (1|subjectNumber)  , data = subset(TEST_change_lg, Condition.F=="0")), digits=4) #control condition

###PERSPECTIVE TAKING
model.WR.coded.persp <- lmer(score.norm ~ Time.F * Condition.F + (1|subjectNumber),data = TEST_perspective_lg, REML = T)
summ(lmer(Normalize(score) ~ Time.F  + (1|subjectNumber)  , data = subset(TEST_perspective_lg, Condition.F=="1")), digits=4) #distanced condition
summ(lmer(Normalize(score) ~ Time.F  + (1|subjectNumber)  , data = subset(TEST_perspective_lg, Condition.F=="0")), digits=4) #control condition

###COMPROMISE
model.WR.coded.compr <- lmer(score.norm ~ Time.F * Condition.F + (1|subjectNumber),data = TEST_compromise_lg, REML = T)
summ(lmer(Normalize(score) ~ Time.F  + (1|subjectNumber)  , data = subset(TEST_compromise_lg, Condition.F=="1")), digits=4) #distanced condition
summ(lmer(Normalize(score) ~ Time.F  + (1|subjectNumber)  , data = subset(TEST_compromise_lg, Condition.F=="0")), digits=4) #control condition

#RESOLUTION OF CONFLICT
model.WR.coded.resol <- lmer(score.norm ~ Time.F * Condition.F + (1|subjectNumber),data = TEST_resolution_lg, REML = T)
summ(lmer(Normalize(score) ~ Time.F  + (1|subjectNumber)  , data = subset(TEST_resolution_lg, Condition.F=="1")), digits=4) #distanced condition
summ(lmer(Normalize(score) ~ Time.F  + (1|subjectNumber)  , data = subset(TEST_resolution_lg, Condition.F=="0")), digits=4) #control condition


#Simple effects (to correct for p-values)
model.WR.codedXx <- lmer(Normalize(score) ~ Time.F * Condition.F*aspect +  (1|subjectNumber)+(1|coder), data = TEST_lg)
test3<-(emmeans(model.WR.codedXx, ~Time.F| Condition.F|aspect)) #sig effect
contrast(test3,interaction=T,adjust="fdr") #to obtain false discovery rate-corrected p-values

test3.5<-(emmeans(model.WR.codedXx, ~ Condition.F|Time.F|aspect)) #sig effect
contrast(test3.5,interaction=T,adjust="fdr") #to obtain false discovery rate-corrected p-values


#LIMITS
emmeans(model.WR.coded.limits, pairwise~Time.F| Condition.F) #sig effect

#CHANGE
emmeans(model.WR.coded.change, pairwise~Time.F| Condition.F) #no differences, trend in the right direcition, but very small

#PERSPECTIVE TAKING
emmeans(model.WR.coded.persp, pairwise~Time.F| Condition.F) #sig effect

#COMPROMISE
emmeans(model.WR.coded.compr, pairwise~Time.F| Condition.F) # #trend in the right direction

#RESOLUTION OF CONFLICT
emmeans(model.WR.coded.resol, pairwise~Time.F| Condition.F) #sig effect


```

## Emo diversity


```{r emotion.scores}

#In this section we create positive and negative emotion scores and create a vector of all emotion variables.

#Create vector of all emotion variable names
emo <- c("InLabMood_1", "InLabMood_2", "InLabMood_3", "InLabMood_4", "InLabMood_5", "InLabMood_6", "InLabMood_7", "InLabMood_8", "InLabMood_9", "InLabMood_10", "InLabMood_11", "InLabMood_12", "InLabMood_13", "InLabMood_14", "InLabMood_15", "InLabMood_16", "InLabMood_21", "InLabMood_22", "InLabMood_23", "InLabMood_24")

#Create vector of only positive emotion variable names
posemo <- c("InLabMood_11", "InLabMood_12", "InLabMood_13", "InLabMood_14", "InLabMood_15", "InLabMood_16", "InLabMood_21", "InLabMood_22", "InLabMood_23", "InLabMood_24")

#Create vector of only negative emotion variable names
negemo <- c("InLabMood_1", "InLabMood_2", "InLabMood_3", "InLabMood_4", "InLabMood_5", "InLabMood_6", "InLabMood_7", "InLabMood_8", "InLabMood_9", "InLabMood_10")

#Create Mean scores for positive and negative emotions.
TEST_lg$posemo.int <- rowMeans(TEST_lg[ , posemo], na.rm = T)
TEST_lg$negemo.int <- rowMeans(TEST_lg[ , negemo], na.rm = T)

```



```{r emotion.entropy}

#Create Shannon's entropy scores for all, positive and negative emotion items.
TEST_lg$glob_emodiv_h <- diversity(TEST_lg[emo], index = "shannon")
TEST_lg$pos_emodiv_h <- diversity(TEST_lg[posemo], index = "shannon")
TEST_lg$neg_emodiv_h <- diversity(TEST_lg[negemo], index = "shannon")

###Examine distributions - HISTOGRAMS

#ALL EMOTION ITEMS
ggplot(TEST_lg,aes(x=glob_emodiv_h)) +
  geom_histogram(colour="black",fill="white") +
  xlab("Shannon's Entropy (Global)") + ylab("Count")

#POSITIVE EMOTION ITEMS
ggplot(TEST_lg,aes(x=pos_emodiv_h)) +
  geom_histogram(colour="black",fill="white") +
  xlab("Shannon's Entropy (Positive)") + ylab("Count")

#NEGATIVE EMOTION ITEMS
ggplot(TEST_lg,aes(x=neg_emodiv_h)) +
  geom_histogram(colour="black",fill="white") +
  xlab("Shannon's Entropy (Negative)") + ylab("Count")

```


```{r entropy.resid}

##Computing (normalized) global emodiversity residuals
##(i.e., regressing out shared variance with negative and positive emotional intensity)

#Get index of all non missing values from the global emotion diversity variable
ed.res <- which(!is.na(TEST$glob_emodiv_h))

TEST$ED.res.h <- NA

#Save residuals for the model but only for rows with non missing global emo diversity scores
TEST$ED.res.h[ed.res] <- residuals.lm(lm(Normalize(glob_emodiv_h) ~ posemo.int + negemo.int, data = TEST), na.rm = T)

##'Computing (normalized) negative emodiversity residuals
##'(i.e., regressing out shared variance with negative emotional intensity)

#Get index of all non missing values from the negative emotion diversity variable
ed.res.neg.lg <- which(!is.na(TEST$neg_emodiv_h))

TEST$ED.neg.res.h <- NA

#Save residuals for the model but only for rows with non missing negative emo diversity scores
TEST$ED.neg.res.h[ed.res.neg.lg] <- residuals.lm(lm(Normalize(neg_emodiv_h) ~ posemo.int + negemo.int, data = TEST), na.rm = T)


##'Computing (normalized) positive emodiversity residuals
##'(i.e., regressing out shared variance with positive emotional intensity)

#Get index of non all non missing values from the positive emotion diversity variable
ed.res.pos <- which(!is.na(TEST$pos_emodiv_h))

TEST$ED.pos.res.h <- NA

#Save residuals for the model but only for rows with non missing positive emo diversity scores
TEST$ED.pos.res.h[ed.res.pos] <- residuals.lm(lm(Normalize(pos_emodiv_h) ~ posemo.int + negemo.int, data = TEST), na.rm = T)

#normalize the emodiversity scores
TEST$ED.neg.res.norm <- Normalize(TEST$ED.neg.res.h)
TEST$ED.pos.res.norm <- Normalize(TEST$ED.pos.res.h)
TEST$ED.res.h.norm <- Normalize(TEST$ED.res.h)


```

```{r subset.emo}
#Convert to long format changing all emotion items from columns to rows.
```

## Mediation

```{r mediation}

#In this section we examine the potential mediation mechanism of condition X time = > neg emodiversity = > wise reasoning

TEST_lg$Time.D.c <- scale(TEST_lg$Time.D, scale = F)
TEST_lg$Condition.D.c <- scale(as.numeric(TEST_lg$Condition.D), scale = F)

TEST_lg$ED.neg.res.norm <- Normalize(TEST_lg$ED.neg.res.h) 

#Creating an interaction term
TEST_lg$Time.D.cXCondition.D.c <- TEST_lg$Time.D.c*TEST_lg$Condition.D.c

model.neg.emo.h <- lmer(ED.neg.res.norm ~ Time.D.c + Condition.D.c + Time.D.cXCondition.D.c + (1|subjectNumber), data = TEST_lg, REML = T)

summary(model.neg.emo.h)
car::Anova(model.neg.emo.h, type = "III")

model.WR.codedX.emodiv <- lmer(score.norm ~ Time.D.c + Condition.D.c + Time.D.cXCondition.D.c + ED.neg.res.norm + (1|subjectNumber), data = TEST_lg, REML = T)

summary(model.WR.codedX.emodiv)

car::Anova(model.WR.codedX.emodiv, type = "III")

summary(mediate(model.neg.emo.h, model.WR.codedX.emodiv, treat = "Time.D.cXCondition.D.c", mediator = "ED.neg.res.norm"))

#wise reasoning as a mediator of training effect on emodiversity
TEST_lg_clean<-subset(TEST_lg,!is.na(score.norm)&!is.na(ED.neg.res.norm))

model.wisdom.mediator <- lmer(score.norm ~ Time.D.c + Condition.D.c + Time.D.cXCondition.D.c + (1|subjectNumber), data = TEST_lg_clean, REML = T)
summ(model.wisdom.mediator)

model.emodiv.via.wisdom <- lmer(ED.neg.res.norm ~ Time.D.c + Condition.D.c + Time.D.cXCondition.D.c + score.norm + (1|subjectNumber), data = TEST_lg_clean, REML = T)
summ(model.emodiv.via.wisdom)
summary(mediation::mediate(model.wisdom.mediator, model.emodiv.via.wisdom, treat = "Time.D.cXCondition.D.c", mediator = "score.norm"),digits=5)

```

## Manipulation Check # 1 (weekly responses on Sundays)

```{r D7.analyses.streams}

#condition 0 and 1 for immersed and distanced and mean center condition 
Output.combined$Condition[Output.combined$Condition.D==1]<-0
Output.combined$Condition[Output.combined$Condition.D==3]<-1
Output.combined$Condition.D<-scale(Output.combined$Condition, scale=F)

###Declare factors
Output.combined$Condition.D.factor <- factor(as.numeric(Output.combined$Condition.D))

#Create total pronoun percent (out of total tokens) variable
Output.combined$Pronoun.perc<-Output.combined$I.perc+Output.combined$We.perc+Output.combined$You.perc+Output.combined$SheHe.perc

#The var I.perc contains a lot of NANs. I turned the NaNs into NAs
Output.combined$I.perc[is.nan(Output.combined$I.perc)] <- NA

#Create third person pro-nouns percent (count of s/he, they, and participnat's name out of total tokens)

Output.combined$Pronountthird.perc<-Output.combined$total.count/Output.combined$Tokens
Output.combined$Third.person.perc<-Output.combined$Pronountthird.perc*100

#Include only reflections with condition information to avoid errors
Output.combined<-subset(Output.combined, Condition==1 | Condition==0)

#Normalize 3rd person and 1st person pronouns (var skewed)
Output.combined$Third.perc.norm<-Normalize(Output.combined$Third.person.perc)
Output.combined$I.perc.norm<-Normalize(Output.combined$I.perc)


#manipulation check for main paper

#ratio

#ratio of third/first percent
#add 1 to I.perc (avoide deviding by 0)
#create ratio variable of third-person percent/first-person percent

Output.combined$immersed.nonzero.perc<-(Output.combined$I.perc+1)

#Ratio "first person pronouns"/"first person+third person pronouns"

Output.combined$immersed.distanced<- Output.combined$I.perc /(Output.combined$Pronountthird.perc + Output.combined$I.perc)
Output.combined$distanced.immersed<- Output.combined$Pronountthird.perc /(Output.combined$Pronountthird.perc + Output.combined$I.perc)

model.immersed.distanced<-lmer(Normalize(immersed.distanced) ~ Condition.D+(1|subjectNumber),data=Output.combined, REML=T)

model.distanced.immersed<-lmer(Normalize(distanced.immersed) ~ Condition.D+(1|subjectNumber),data=Output.combined, REML=T)

summ(model.distanced.immersed, digits=3)
emmeans(model.distanced.immersed,~Condition.D)

summ(model.immersed.distanced)

#Descriptives

Output.combined %>% 
  group_by(Condition) %>% 
  dplyr::summarize(mean_ratio=mean(immersed.distanced, na.rm = TRUE),n=n(), sd=sd(immersed.distanced, na.rm = TRUE),se=sd/sqrt(n))

```

```{r test mediation}
#In this chunk we convert our existing dataset to long format with the coded wisdom scores for each dimension and coder converted from columns to rows

#Convert to long

#In this chunk we created new recoded variables for coders and wisdom dimensions

TEST_lg$coder[TEST_lg$dimension == "Compromise_OT"] <- 0
TEST_lg$coder[TEST_lg$dimension == "Search_for_Resolution_NJ"] <- 1
TEST_lg$coder[TEST_lg$dimension == "Search_for_Resolution_OT"] <- 0

##Create a new variable "aspect" which will contain a character vector for each wisdom dimension
TEST_lg$aspect[TEST_lg$dimension=="Limits_NJ"] <- "IH"
TEST_lg$aspect[TEST_lg$dimension=="Limits_OT"] <- "IH"
TEST_lg$aspect[TEST_lg$dimension=="Change_NJ"] <- "Chg"
TEST_lg$aspect[TEST_lg$dimension=="Change_OT"] <- "Chg"
TEST_lg$aspect[TEST_lg$dimension=="Perspective_Taking_NJ"] <- "Prsp"
TEST_lg$aspect[TEST_lg$dimension=="Perspective_Taking_OT"] <- "Prsp"
TEST_lg$aspect[TEST_lg$dimension=="Compromise_NJ"] <- "Comp"
TEST_lg$aspect[TEST_lg$dimension=="Compromise_OT"] <- "Comp"
TEST_lg$aspect[TEST_lg$dimension=="Search_for_Resolution_NJ"] <- "Reso"
TEST_lg$aspect[TEST_lg$dimension=="Search_for_Resolution_OT"] <- "Reso"


#Here check the skew of coded wisdom scores and use the Normalize function to create a new less skewed variable  

#histogram of score
hist(TEST_lg$score) #variable skewed 

#Normalized histogram of score
hist(Normalize(TEST_lg$score)) # use normalize function below, though still skewed

#Create a new score.norm variable that contains the Normalized scores
TEST_lg$score.norm <- Normalize(TEST_lg$score)

#Creating an interaction term
TEST_lg$Time.D.cXCondition.D.c <- scale(TEST_lg$Time.D,scale=F)*scale(TEST_lg$Condition.D,scale=F)
TEST_lg$Time.D.c<-scale(TEST_lg$Time.D,scale=F)
TEST_lg$Condition.D.c<-scale(TEST_lg$Condition.D,scale=F)

model.we.i <- lmer(we.i.perc.norm ~ Time.D.c + Condition.D.c + Time.D.cXCondition.D.c + (1|subjectNumber), data = TEST_lg, REML = T)
summ(model.we.i)

model.WR.codedX.we.i <- lmer(score.norm ~ Time.D.c + Condition.D.c + Time.D.cXCondition.D.c + we.i.perc.norm + (1|subjectNumber), data = TEST_lg, REML = T)
summ(model.WR.codedX.we.i, digits=4)

summary(mediation::mediate(model.we.i, model.WR.codedX.we.i, treat = "Time.D.cXCondition.D.c", mediator = "we.i.perc.norm", sim=3000),digits=4)


#scaled variables (to get standartized estimate)


#Creating an interaction term
TEST_lg$Time.D.cXCondition.S <- scale(TEST_lg$Time.D)*scale(TEST_lg$Condition.D)
TEST_lg$Time.D.S<-scale(TEST_lg$Time.D)
TEST_lg$Condition.S<-scale(TEST_lg$Condition.D)
TEST_lg$we.i.perc.norm.S<-scale(TEST_lg$we.i.perc.norm)
TEST_lg$score.norm.S<-scale(TEST_lg$score.norm)

model.we.i <- lmer(we.i.perc.norm.S ~ Time.D.S + Condition.S + Time.D.cXCondition.S + (1|subjectNumber), data = TEST_lg, REML = T)
summ(model.we.i)

model.WR.codedX.we.i <- lmer(score.norm.S ~ Time.D.S + Condition.S + Time.D.cXCondition.S + we.i.perc.norm.S + (1|subjectNumber), data = TEST_lg, REML = T)
summ(model.WR.codedX.we.i, digits=4)

summary(mediation::mediate(model.we.i, model.WR.codedX.we.i, treat = "Time.D.cXCondition.S", mediator = "we.i.perc.norm.S", sim=3000),digits=4) #rsq = .01




#just examine intervention condition and use scaled variables
TEST_lg1<-subset(TEST_lg,Condition.D=="1")
TEST_lg1$we.i.perc.norm<-Normalize(TEST_lg1$we.i.perc)
TEST_lg1$score.norm<-Normalize(TEST_lg1$score)
TEST_lg1$Time.C<-scale(TEST_lg1$Time.D.c, scale=F)


model.we.i.INT <-lmer(we.i.perc.norm ~ Time.C   + (1|subjectNumber), data = TEST_lg1, REML = T)
summ(model.we.i.INT, digits=5) #r sq = 0.02510==>r = 0.1584298
model.WR.codedX.we.i.INT <- lmer(score.norm ~ Time.C + we.i.perc.norm + (1|subjectNumber), data = TEST_lg1, REML = T)
summ(model.WR.codedX.we.i.INT, digits=4) #total r sq = 0.0234
model.WR.codedX.we.i.T.INT <- lmer(score.norm ~ Time.C +  (1|subjectNumber), data = TEST_lg1, REML = T)
summ(model.WR.codedX.we.i.T.INT, digits=4) #total r sq = 0.0137
#thus, partial Rsq in scores due to we.i is = 0.0234 -0.0137  = 0.001=>r = 0.10
summ(lmer(score.norm ~ we.i.perc.norm +  (1|subjectNumber), data = TEST_lg1, REML = T), digits=5) #rsq = 0.01608
#thus, partial Rsq in scores due to Time, when accounting for we.i is = 0.0234 -0.01608  = 0.007


#thus, product a*b of partial correlations would be = 0.0128709
mediation.INT<-mediation::mediate(model.we.i.INT, model.WR.codedX.we.i.INT, treat = "Time.C", mediator = "we.i.perc.norm", sim=5000, conf.level = 0.90)
summary(mediation.INT)
```

## Self Reported Wisdom Analyses

```{r main.effect.swis}

###In this section we test the main effect using self reported (as opposed to coded) wisdom as the dependent variable

#Gather the names of all scale items into a single character vector
SWIS <- c("SWSa_1","SWSa_2","SWSa_3","SWSa_4","SWSa_5","SWSa_6","SWSa_7","SWSa_8","SWSb_1","SWSb_2","SWSb_3","SWSb_4","SWSb_5","SWSb_6","SWSc_1","SWSc_2","SWSc_3")

#Convert data from wide to long such that each SWIS variable is now a row 
TEST.lgSWIS <- gather(TEST, key = "question", value = "score", SWIS, na.rm = T)

TEST.lgSWIS$adverse.c <- scale(TEST.lgSWIS$adverse.events, scale = F)

#Check distribution of SWIS scores
hist(TEST.lgSWIS$score) #variable OK

#Normalize SWIS scores
TEST.lgSWIS$score.norm <- Normalize(TEST.lgSWIS$score)

#Examine effect of condition on SWIS (all items, but outsider viewpoint, as it is not accessed via content analysis)
model.SWIS <- lmer(score.norm ~ Time.F * Condition.F + same.person+where.code+event.code.final+(1|subjectNumber) + (1|question), data = TEST.lgSWIS, REML = T)

summ(model.SWIS, center = "all", digits = 4)

#marginal interaction: 
emmeans(model.SWIS, pairwise~Time.F| Condition.F) #sig effect: sig decline in control, but no decline in training

#sig negative effect of time in the control condition - less self-reported wise reasoning compared to before the intervention
#no significant effect for the training group - i..e, maintenance of wise reasoning compared to before the intervention

#3 way interaction with adversity
model.SWIS.adv <- lmer(score.norm ~ Time.F * Condition.F * adverse.c + (1|subjectNumber) + (1|question), data = TEST.lgSWIS, REML=T)
summ(model.SWIS.adv, center = "all", digits = 4)
#sig interaction: 
emmeans(model.SWIS.adv, pairwise~Time.F| Condition.F) #sig effect: sig decline in control, but no decline in training

#try Bayesian model - ordinal DV

model.swiss.bayes <- brm(score+1 ~ Time.F * Condition.F + (1|subjectNumber) + (1|question), data = TEST.lgSWIS,  family = acat())
summary(model.swiss.bayes)
conditions <- make_conditions(model.swiss.bayes, "Condition.F")
plot(conditional_effects(model.swiss.bayes, "Time.F",conditions=conditions,categorical=T),plot = FALSE)[[1]] + 
  theme_nice() + theme(legend.title = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom") + scale_x_discrete(labels = c("Before", "After")) +scale_color_colorblind() +
  scale_fill_colorblind()

emmeans(model.swiss.bayes, pairwise~Time.F| Condition.F, level = .95) #sig decline in the immersed condition / maintenance in the distant self-condition



```

## SWIS Dimensions

```{r main.effect.swis.dimensions}

#In this section we test the main interaction finding for each subcomponent of SWIS

###PERSPECTIVE TAKING

#Create a list of sub-scale variable names
perspect <- c("SWSa_1", "SWSa_2", "SWSa_3", "SWSa_4")

#Create a long version using just the items from the SWIS sub-component
TEST.lgSWIS.perspect <- gather(TEST, key = "question", value = "score", perspect, na.rm = T)

#run bayesian model with perspective as an ordinal variable
model.swiss.perspect.bayes <- brm(score+1 ~ Time.F * Condition.F + (1|subjectNumber) , data = TEST.lgSWIS.perspect,  family = acat())
summary(model.swiss.perspect.bayes) #no significant effect
emmeans(model.swiss.perspect.bayes, pairwise~Time.F| Condition.F) #trend toward decline in the immersed condition / improvement in the distant self-condition


#run a general linear model, normalizing the distribution of the scores first
TEST.lgSWIS.perspect$score.norm <- Normalize(TEST.lgSWIS.perspect$score)
#Fit model
model.SWIS.perspect <- lmer(score.norm ~ Time.F * Condition.F + (1|subjectNumber) + (1|question), data = TEST.lgSWIS.perspect, REML = T)
summ(model.SWIS.perspect)
#Marginal interaction
emmeans(model.SWIS.perspect, pairwise~Time.F| Condition.F) #simple effects
#negative trend of time in the control condition - less self-reported perspective-taking compared to before the intervention
#positive trend of time in the self-distanced group - more self-reported perspective-taking compared to before the intervention


###CHANGE

#Create a list of sub-scale variable names
change <- c("SWSa_5", "SWSa_6", "SWSa_7", "SWSa_8")

#Create a long version using just the items from the SWIS sub-component
TEST.lgSWIS.change <- gather(TEST, key = "question", value = "score", change, na.rm = T)

#run bayesian model with perspective as an ordinal variable
model.swiss.change.bayes <- brm(score+1 ~ Time.F * Condition.F + (1|subjectNumber) , data = TEST.lgSWIS.change,  family = acat())
summary(model.swiss.change.bayes)
emmeans(model.swiss.change.bayes, pairwise~Time.F| Condition.F) #trend toward decline in the immersed condition / sig change in the distant self-condition (mostly because more change predicted at t1 in the distant self group at the beginning)

#run a general linear model, normalizing the distribution of the scores first
TEST.lgSWIS.change$score.norm <- Normalize(TEST.lgSWIS.change$score)
#Fit model
model.SWIS.change <- lmer(score.norm ~ Time.F*Condition.F + (1|subjectNumber) + (1|question), data = TEST.lgSWIS.change, REML = T)
summ(model.SWIS.change)
#no condition effect, but decline in change over time.

#INTELLECTUAL HUMILITY

humility <- c("SWSb_1", "SWSb_2", "SWSb_3", "SWSb_4")

TEST.lgSWIS.humility <- gather(TEST, key = "question", value = "score", humility, na.rm = T)

#run bayesian model with perspective as an ordinal variable
model.swiss.humility.bayes <- brm(score+1 ~ Time.F * Condition.F + (1|subjectNumber), data = TEST.lgSWIS.humility,  family = acat())
summary(model.swiss.humility.bayes)
emmeans(model.swiss.humility.bayes, pairwise~Time.F| Condition.F) #sig  decline in the immersed condition / improvement in the distant self-condition

#run a general linear model, normalizing the distribution of the scores first
TEST.lgSWIS.humility$score.norm <- Normalize(TEST.lgSWIS.humility$score)
model.SWIS.humility <- lmer(score.norm ~ Time.F*Condition.F + (1|subjectNumber) + (1|question), data = TEST.lgSWIS.humility, REML = T)

summ(model.SWIS.humility)

#no interaction but a trend
#marginal interaction: 
emmeans(model.SWIS.humility, pairwise~Time.F| Condition.F) #simple effects
#marg sig negative effect of time in the control condition - less self-reported focus on limits of knowledge compared to before the intervention
#no diff in the self-distanced condition - maintenance over time


###RESOLUTION OF CONFLICT

resol <- c("SWSb_5", "SWSb_6", "SWSc_1", "SWSc_2", "SWSc_3")

TEST.lgSWIS.resol <- gather(TEST, key = "question", value = "score", resol, na.rm = T)

#run bayesian model with perspective as an ordinal variable
model.swiss.resol.bayes <- brm(score+1 ~ Time.F * Condition.F + (1|subjectNumber), data = TEST.lgSWIS.resol,  family = acat())
summary(model.swiss.resol.bayes)
emmeans(model.swiss.resol.bayes, pairwise~Time.F| Condition.F, level = .90) #sig decline in the immersed condition / no change in the distant self-condition

#run a general linear model, normalizing the distribution of the scores first
TEST.lgSWIS.resol$score.norm <- Normalize(TEST.lgSWIS.resol$score)

model.SWIS.resol <- lmer(score.norm ~ Time.F*Condition.F + (1|subjectNumber) + (1|question), data = TEST.lgSWIS.resol, REML = T)

summ(model.SWIS.resol)

#no interaction but a trend: 
emmeans(model.SWIS.resol, pairwise~Time.F| Condition.F) #simple effects
#sig negative effect of time in the control condition - less self-reported focus on compromise and conflict resolution compared to before the intervention
#no diff in the self-distanced condition - maintenance over time

###OUTSIDER PERSPECTIVE
#additional test of outsider viewpoint (not assessed in narrative streams)
outsider <- c("SWSc_4", "SWSc_5", "SWSc_6", "SWSc_7")

TEST.lgSWIS.outsider <- gather(TEST, key = "question", value = "score", outsider, na.rm = T)

summ(model.SWIS.outsider)
#nothing here

library(brms)
model.swiss.outsider.bayes <- brm(score+1 ~ Time.F * Condition.F + (1|subjectNumber), data = TEST.lgSWIS.outsider,  family = acat())
summary(model.swiss.outsider.bayes)
conditions <- make_conditions(model.swiss.bayes, "Condition.F")
plot(conditional_effects(model.swiss.bayes, "Time.F",conditions=conditions,categorical=T),plot = FALSE)[[1]] +

  scale_fill_colorblind()

emmeans(model.swiss.bayes, pairwise~Time.F| Condition.F, level = .95) #sig decline in the immersed condition / maintenance in the distant self-condition
```
